name: Tirumala Venkateswara Temple
famous_for: World's most visited Hindu temple atop the sacred Seven Hills of Seshachalam
short_description: Perched on the sacred Venkatadri hill of the Seshachalam range, Tirumala is dedicated to Lord Venkateswara (Balaji).
full_description: Known as Kaliyuga Vaikuntam, Tirumala Venkateswara Temple has been patronized across millennia by the Pallavas, Cholas, and Vijayanagara emperor Sri Krishnadevaraya.

history.short_history: Puranic manifestation of Lord Vishnu as Venkateswara residing on the sacred Venkatadri peak.
history.detailed_history: Mentioned in early Tamil Sangam literature as Vengadam and enriched by the Vijayanagara empire.
history.cultural_significance: Celebrates the annual 9-day Brahmotsavam festival drawing millions of devotees.
history.religious_significance: One of the 108 sacred Divya Desams where Lord Srinivasa manifested in self-formed Svayambhu deity.

name: Ananthagiri Hills
famous_for: Dense Eastern Ghats forest trails, birthplace of River Musi, and Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy Temple
short_description: Ananthagiri Hills is Telangana's prime dense forest getaway, located just 75 km from Hyderabad.
full_description: Featuring scenic sunrise viewpoints, medicinal herb flora, tranquil coffee and teak plantations, and historic temple caves.

history.short_history: Ancient forest hermitage where Sage Markandeya performed penance.
history.detailed_history: Built in the early 17th century by the Nizams of Hyderabad as a serene summer convalescence sanatorium.
history.cultural_significance: Epicenter of Telangana eco-tourism and nature conservation.
history.religious_significance: Sacred cave shrine of Sri Anantha Padmanabha Swamy.

images.caption: Misty canopy trails of Ananthagiri forest reserve

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
famous_for: 14 monumental multi-tiered gopurams, Hall of Thousand Pillars, and Golden Lotus tank
short_description: Historic Hindu temple situated on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in the ancient temple city of Madurai.
full_description: Dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva), the complex boasts 14 magnificent gopurams reaching up to 52 meters high.

history.short_history: Founded in early Pandyan antiquity and reconstructed under Nayaka rulers.
history.detailed_history: Rebuilt by King Viswanatha Nayak in the 16th-17th centuries following Shilpa Shastra guidelines.
history.cultural_significance: Hosts the spectacular 10-day Chithirai Festival celebrating divine wedding.
history.religious_significance: One of the supreme Shakti and Shaivite sacred power centers of South India.

images.caption: Intricately sculpted colorful gopuram of Meenakshi Amman Temple

name: Hampi
famous_for: UNESCO World Heritage ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire, Stone Chariot, and Virupaksha Temple
short_description: Hampi is a surreal landscape of giant granite boulders, 14th-century royal palaces, musical pillared halls, and the Tungabhadra River.
full_description: The capital of the glorious Vijayanagara Empire in the 14th to 16th centuries, Hampi was one of the wealthiest cities in the medieval world.

history.short_history: Puranic Kishkindha kingdom from the Ramayana, later imperial capital of Vijayanagara from 1336 CE.
history.detailed_history: Flourished under emperor Krishnadevaraya before the Battle of Talikota in 1565 CE.
history.cultural_significance: Celebrates the annual Hampi Utsav showcasing Karnataka classical arts.
history.religious_significance: Continuous worship at the 7th-century Virupaksha Temple honoring Lord Shiva.

images.caption: Iconic monolithic Stone Chariot at Vijaya Vittala Temple, Hampi

name: Rishikesh
famous_for: Yoga Capital of the World, White water Ganga rafting, Lakshman Jhula, and Triveni Ghat Aarti
short_description: Nestled in the Himalayan foothills where the sacred Ganges emerges onto the Northern Plains.
full_description: Rishikesh attracts spiritual seekers, yogis, and adventure enthusiasts worldwide with ashrams, suspension bridges, and cliff jumping.

history.short_history: Named after Hrishikesha (Lord Vishnu) who appeared to Sage Raibhya after severe austerities.
history.detailed_history: Global yoga center popularized internationally when The Beatles visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi's ashram in 1968.
history.cultural_significance: Hosts the International Yoga Festival annually along the holy Ganga.
history.religious_significance: Gateway to the sacred Char Dham Himalayan pilgrimage circuit.

images.caption: Evening Ganga Aarti glow at Triveni Ghat, Rishikesh

name: Puri Jagannath Temple & Golden Beach
famous_for: One of the Four Maha Char Dham pilgrimage sites, annual Ratha Yatra chariot festival, and Blue Flag Golden Beach
short_description: Puri is the eternal abode of Lord Jagannath on the Bay of Bengal coast in Odisha.
full_description: The 12th-century Jagannath Temple is famous for its monumental 65-meter deula, massive Mahaprasad Ananda Bazar, and sacred wooden neem deities.

history.short_history: Constructed by King Anantavarman Chodaganga Deva of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in the 12th century.
history.detailed_history: Puranic origins connected with King Indradyumna and the mystical Daru Brahma.
history.cultural_significance: Home to the world's largest religious procession — the sacred Ratha Yatra.
history.religious_significance: One of the four prime Maha Char Dhams established across the four cardinal corners of India.

images.caption: Monumental Spire of Sri Jagannath Temple at Puri
